entries.summary: Reuters independently corroborates overnight Nasdaq futures weakness near -0.3% versus flat S&P futures, while Asian chip shares rally. No material change to the cautious reversal thesis.
bullish: AP-confirmed Nasdaq Composite +6.5% and S&P 500 +4.7% close; strong recovery beyond intraday estimates.
Nvidia +31.48% close at $165.05, broad chip participation according to Barron's.
MarketWatch reported VIX down over 19% near 29 and VXN down 18% near 37 intraday; exact closes unavailable.
Russell 2000 +3.40% and Micron +19.04% at Monday close support participation beyond Nvidia.
Reuters syndicated report shows Asian equities rebounding sharply, including Taiwan and South Korea; international semiconductor sentiment improves.
AP independently corroborates Asian chip-led recovery; Reuters reports oil down more than 3%.
bearish: Unusually sharp rebound may reflect short-covering; Tuesday follow-through not yet observed.
10Y intraday 4.95% and unresolved Fed repricing create valuation sensitivity; matched 2Y unavailable.
AI export and governance risks persist; synchronized SOX, QQQ, cash breadth and matched oil quotes missing.
Reuters reports hawkish Fed bets and rising yields; VIX remains elevated despite decline.
Reuters reports December tightening fully priced and 2Y/10Y yields elevated; exact primary FedWatch probability unavailable.
Reported Nasdaq futures gains faded from +0.58% to +0.05% between 01:30 and 02:30 UTC; not a cash reversal.
Secondary 03:30 UTC report shows NQ -0.33% versus ES -0.07%; modest overnight relative weakness, not cash confirmation.
Reuters Morning Bid corroborates Nasdaq futures around -0.3% versus flat S&P futures; not a fresh cash reversal.

editorial.marketOverview: Monday's sharp US technology rebound remains the starting point. Asian semiconductor gains corroborate improved sentiment, but overnight US futures lag broader equity futures. Official QQQ/SOX closes and direct breadth remain unavailable; prior small-cap gains are a breadth proxy only.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters Morning Bid independently reports Nasdaq futures down around 0.3% versus flat S&P futures, consistent with the earlier secondary report rather than a new deterioration. Taiwan shares rose over 9%, with major suppliers reaching trading limits. Open Watch remains unchanged at 177 events; no new isolated catalyst reaction is established.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Reuters reports a quarter-point December hike fully priced with some risk of a larger move. The earlier reported Treasury pair implies 24.98 bp, not a synchronized live curve. Oil softness may relieve inflation pressure but conflicting Brent quotes and unspecified contracts preclude a precise comparison. The futures pullback does not yet invalidate Monday's reversal.
editorial.threeDayPath: Tuesday November 24 tests whether Monday gains hold through ADI, consumer confidence and Dell/HP after close. Wednesday November 25 brings GDP, PCE, claims and Beige Book, plus earnings reactions. Thursday is closed; Friday November 27 closes at 13:00 ET, with thin liquidity amplifying moves. Cautious bullish reversal remains the base case, not a forecast of uninterrupted gains.
editorial.bullCase: A stabilization in futures followed by cash semiconductor outperformance and improving breadth would support continuation. Softer inflation and steady yields could help, while constructive earnings commentary would reinforce demand expectations.
editorial.bearCase: A renewed chip-led selloff, rising front-end yields or disappointing earnings could unwind Monday's squeeze. China export and order risks remain unresolved. A broad reversal erasing most Monday gains would invalidate the recovery thesis.
editorial.watchNext: Verify QQQ and SOX cash relative strength, advance-decline breadth, official VXN/VIX, synchronized Treasury yields, CME FedWatch and matched oil contracts. Monitor ADI, consumer confidence, Dell and HP, Wednesday macro and Friday shortened trading. Do not equate overnight indications with realized cash returns.
